title: Perceptrons and backpropagation
subtitle: One neuron draws a line. Stack layers and the network can draw any boundary — if you can train it.

neuron.title: The artificial neuron
neuron.body: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias, z = Σ wᵢxᵢ + b, then applies an activation function: step (perceptron), sigmoid 1/(1+e⁻ᶻ), tanh, or ReLU max(0, z). Without a non-linearity, any stack of layers collapses into one linear map.

perc.title: What one neuron can and cannot do
perc.body: A perceptron’s decision boundary is a straight line (hyperplane). It learns AND (converged: yes) but cannot learn XOR — Minsky and Papert’s 1969 observation which stalled the field. The cure is a hidden layer.

mlp.title: Multilayer networks and backpropagation
mlp.body: A multilayer perceptron has hidden layers between input and output. Backpropagation trains it: (1) forward pass computes the output; (2) the loss measures the error; (3) the chain rule sends the error gradient backwards, layer by layer, giving ∂L/∂w for every weight; (4) gradient descent updates w ← w − η ∂L/∂w. Run the 2-3-1 network on XOR: the loss falls to 0.0004 and all four outputs are right (yes).
mlp.steps: Output unit: y = σ(z), loss E = ½(y − t)². Its error signal is δ = (y − t)·y(1 − y). For a hidden unit h the signal is passed back through the weight: δ_h = δ_o · w · h(1 − h). Each weight moves against its gradient: Δw = −η δ · (input to that weight).

deep.title: Deep learning and architectures
deep.body: Deep learning uses many layers that learn features automatically. Convolutional networks share small filters across an image (translation-invariant features); recurrent networks carry a hidden state through a sequence; transformers replace recurrence with attention. Universal approximation: one hidden layer of enough units can approximate any continuous function — depth makes it efficient. Generative networks (GANs, diffusion models, language models) create new data.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Neuron = weighted sum + activation; a single neuron separates linearly only.
  • Hidden layers + backpropagation solve XOR and far more.
